display.purpose: Console monograms on blocks (2.6rem strip, 3.4rem library, 4rem console header), with a stepped extrusion.

headline.purpose: Page titles (Libreria, Opzioni) with a two-step hard extrusion.

title.purpose: Selected game in the cover flow and showcase; max 22-24ch, balanced.

body-strong.purpose: Nav pills, box titles (two-line clamp), console names, buttons.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focusable element: a dark gap in the set hue, then white. Paired with object motion.

shadows.name: focus-ring-field
shadows.purpose: Search field while typing: the yellow says 'type here'.

shadows.name: focus-ring-inset
shadows.purpose: Grid boxcards, whose paint is clipped by content-visibility.

shadows.name: yellow-ledge
shadows.purpose: Retry button at rest; pressed it drops to 0 1px 0.

shadows.name: logo-extrusion
shadows.purpose: The yellow Mate tag in the logo.

shadows.name: monogram-extrusion
shadows.value: -1px 1px 0 oklch(0.4 0.19 var(--bh)), -2px 2px 0 oklch(0.4 0.19 var(--bh)), -3px 3px 0 oklch(0.36 0.18 var(--bh)), -4px 4px 0 oklch(0.32 0.17 var(--bh))

shadows.name: contact-shadow
shadows.purpose: Fan cards: objects resting above the floor.

shadows.name: flow-lift
shadows.purpose: Ring and deep drop behind the focused cover-flow box (6px outside it).

shadows.name: glass-lip
shadows.purpose: Top edge of the Options panel.

shadows.name: daisy-rim
shadows.purpose: The gamepad keyboard disc: a solid rim plus a deep drop.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Every UI transition, the camera, the cover-flow slide, fast turntable swaps.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Physical objects settling: block lift (300ms), fan (360ms, 30ms stagger), boxcard square-up (340ms), turntable swing-in (620ms). Overshoot is deliberate.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The newly selected cover-flow box (420ms): a smaller overshoot than spring.

motion.name: backdrop-relight
motion.purpose: The set re-lights to the focused hue; the only place the hue animates.

motion.name: camera
motion.purpose: View Transition between pages: in = old page passes the camera (translateZ 300px, blur 8px), new arrives from -480px; out reverses.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: Crossfade when a font pairing restyles the whole page.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Nav pills and font cards on press.

motion.name: sway
motion.purpose: The selected cover-flow box and the showcase turntable idle-sway (rotateY -16 to 12deg).

motion.name: daisy-enter
motion.value: opacity 180ms ease-out, transform 240ms ease (from translateY(-10px) scale(0.94)); exit 150ms
motion.purpose: Gamepad keyboard opens and leaves faster than it came.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Flights, sways and springs off (1ms); cross-document view transitions off; state changes stay instant and visible.

narrative.overview:
RetroMate is a shop window. Every game is a physical box standing on a seamless coloured photo set, and the set is lit in the hue of whatever has focus: move onto a Game Boy Advance title and the whole backdrop turns violet, onto a Mega Drive game and it swings to cyan. The library is browsed the way a collector looks at a display: boxes at their real packaging proportions, consoles as solid blocks with their games fanned out of the top, a cover flow of recently played boxes on Home, and a camera that flies forward into a deeper page and pulls back out of it.

Objects behave physically. Boxes are true six-faced 3D (cardboard for Nintendo, black plastic cases with a rim and a gloss for Mega Drive and PS2), console blocks are oblique cuboids whose depth faces extrude when lifted, grid boxes stand turned 30 degrees to show their spine and square up to face you when selected. Chrome is quiet and flat on top of this: white ink, translucent veils, one action yellow. The system is built for a gamepad first and a TV across the room, so focus is never subtle: a dark gap, a white ring, and the object itself moves.

The system refuses the flat grid of rectangular covers that every ROM manager ships. A game is never a thumbnail in a tile; it is an object on a set.
keyCharacteristics: A vivid oklch backdrop driven by one per-console hue, re-lit on every focus change.
White ink everywhere; one action yellow (#ffe14d) with a darker extruded edge.
Fake 3D throughout: preserve-3d boxes at real millimetre proportions, skewed cuboid blocks, hard offset extrusions instead of blurred shadows.
Focus is a dark gap plus a white ring, and the focused object lifts, squares up or faces the viewer.
A View Transition camera: deeper pages fly forward, back pulls away.
Five self-hosted sans-serif pairings, swapped at runtime through display/body variables.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: Action Yellow appears only where a press does something or on the logo tag. It is never a decorative fill, a border for its own sake, or a heading colour.

rules.name: The Hue Follows Focus Rule
rules.body: Chrome never hard-codes a hue. The set, panels, focus gap, legend and gamepad keyboard all derive from `--hue`, which app.js sets to the console hue of the focused object. Only the backdrop animates the change (800ms, through a non-inherited copy), so the rest of the page never recalculates per frame.

rules.name: The White Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on the set is white or Ink Soft. Ink Dark exists only on yellow and white surfaces.

rules.name: The Pairing Is A Variable Rule
rules.body: No component names a font family. Display text uses `--f-display`, `--fw-display`, `--fs-display` and `--ls-display`; everything else uses `--f-body`. A new screen must look right in all five pairings.

rules.name: The Display Is For Names Rule
rules.body: The display face is reserved for names of things: headings, the logo, console monograms, game titles and the cover fallback printed on a box without art. Labels, counts and controls stay in the body face.

rules.name: The Extrusion Not Blur Rule
rules.body: Chrome and type get hard offset extrusions in a darker tone of their own colour. Blurred shadows are reserved for objects resting on the floor.

rules.name: The Real Proportions Rule
rules.body: A box's width, height and depth come from the console's real packaging in millimetres (GBA/GBC/GB 125 x 125 x 23, NES 127 x 178 x 38, SNES 160 x 195 x 29, Mega Drive 152 x 195 x 25, PS2 135 x 190 x 15), never from the cover art, so boxes keep their size when art loads or is missing.

rules.name: The Physical Spring Rule
rules.body: `--spring` (cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.32, 0.64, 1)) and `--settle` (cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.12, 0.5, 1)) are for physical objects settling: blocks lifting, fans opening, grid boxes squaring up, the turntable swinging in, the selected cover-flow box. Their small overshoot is deliberate. Everything else uses `--ease` (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)). Reduced motion turns flights, sways and springs off and keeps state changes instant and visible.

dos: Do set `--hue` from the focused object's console hue and derive every chrome colour from it.
Do show focus as the 3px dark gap plus 3px white ring (`--ring`) and move the object as well: lift, square up or face the viewer.
Do size every box from the console's real packaging millimetres through `--ar` and `--d`.
Do use `--spring` or `--settle` only for physical objects settling, and `--ease` for every UI transition.
Do use the display variables (`--f-display`, `--fw-display`, `--fs-display`, `--ls-display`) for names and `--f-body` for everything else, and check new screens in all five pairings.
Do give flat surfaces depth with hard bottom-left extrusions in a darker tone of their own colour.
Do fly the camera forward into deeper pages and pull it back on return, and turn flights and sways off under reduced motion.
donts: Don't lay games out as a flat grid of rectangular cover thumbnails; a game is always a box on the set.
Don't use Action Yellow for decoration; it marks only what a press will do, and the logo tag.
Don't rely on colour alone for focus or selection.
Don't put blurred drop shadows under chrome; soft shadows belong only beneath objects on the floor.
Don't apply spring or settle overshoot to nav pills, fields, cards or the legend.
Don't hard-code a font family or a console hue in a component.
Don't animate `--hue` anywhere except the backdrop.
